# Power Words Bank

Words that carry above-average curiosity or emotional weight in Billy's research outlier set. Two categories: Global (pull on almost any audience) and Audience-Specific (resonate uniquely for the AI-for-creators / business-owner audience). Mined from the full title set across all 11 channels. One word per entry.

Loaded by `vid-title` for headlines, `vid-intro` for hooks, `vid-thumbnail` for thumbnail text.

## How to read this bank

Each entry is a single word or phrase + when it lands + when it fails + a real worked example linked to [[pattern-bank]]. No frequency or channel counts: those anchor on "appeared most" instead of "fits this line." Decide by fit, not popularity. Edit in place: delete words you wouldn't say, add words you prefer.

## Global power words

### "STOP"
- When it lands: a contrarian command where you have the authority to push back AND a replacement to offer.
- When it fails: scolding with no "do this instead." Reads as nagging.
- Worked example: "Stop Using Nano Banana Pro WRONG (Do This Instead)" → [[pattern-bank]] (@brockmesarich)

### "DON'T"
- When it lands: paired with the better path. "DON'T [X], do [Y]."
- When it fails: a blanket "don't" with no alternative.
- Worked example: "DON'T Sell AI Agents, Sell AI Micro-Apps Instead!" → [[pattern-bank]] (@duncanrogoff)

### "WRONG"
- When it lands: naming a common mistake the viewer suspects they're making.
- When it fails: when you can't show what "right" looks like in the video.
- Worked example: "95% of People STILL Prompt ChatGPT-5 Wrong" → [[pattern-bank]] (@jeffsu)

### "JUST"
- When it lands: signals freshness on a release ("Just Dropped," "Just Changed").
- When it fails: when the thing isn't actually new. Burns trust.
- Worked example: "Anthropic Just Dropped Claude for Small Businesses" → [[pattern-bank]] (@brockmesarich)

### "FOREVER"
- When it lands: stakes-raiser on a genuine shift ("changed X forever").
- When it fails: on incremental updates. Overpromises.
- Worked example: "Claude Just Changed Making YouTube Videos Forever" → [[pattern-bank]] (@ed-lawrence)

### "BETTER"
- When it lands: status hook, joining the skilled minority ("better than 99%").
- When it fails: when the video doesn't show the gap between the 1% and the rest.
- Worked example: "How to Use Claude Cowork Better Than 99% of People" → [[pattern-bank]] (@brockmesarich)

### "MASTER"
- When it lands: promises competence on something the viewer finds intimidating.
- When it fails: on a trivial topic where "master" feels inflated.
- Worked example: "Master 95% of Claude Design in 17 Minutes" → [[pattern-bank]] (@brockmesarich)

### "ONLY"
- When it lands: ends the search. "The only X you'll ever need."
- When it fails: on fast-changing topics where "only" is obviously false.
- Worked example: "The only AutoResearch tutorial you'll ever need" → [[pattern-bank]] (@davidondrej)

### "FREE"
- When it lands: removes the cost objection, especially against a known paid tool.
- When it fails: when "free" needs heavy asterisks. Bait-and-switch reads cheap.
- Worked example: "You NEED to Use n8n RIGHT NOW!! (Free, Local, Private)" → [[pattern-bank]] (@networkchuck)

### "NEW"
- When it lands: novelty on tools or skills the audience tracks.
- When it fails: when the "new" thing is repackaged old.
- Worked example: "5 NEW AI That Just Changed YouTube Forever" → [[pattern-bank]] (@ed-lawrence)

### "STEAL"
- When it lands: generosity signal, you're handing over a real asset.
- When it fails: when there's nothing concrete to take.
- Worked example: "15 Claude Cowork Skills I Can't Live Without (steal them)" → [[pattern-bank]] (@brockmesarich)

### "WITHOUT"
- When it lands: removes the dreaded cost (no team, no budget, no slop).
- When it fails: when the "without" isn't actually a real fear for the viewer.
- Worked example: "How I Use Claude Code to Build a Profitable Personal Brand Without a Team" → [[pattern-bank]] (@duncanrogoff)

### "BEST"
- When it lands: a definitive claim that flips an underdog ("introverts make the BEST").
- When it fails: generic "best tips" with no specific subject.
- Worked example: "Why Introverts Make the BEST Content Creators" → [[pattern-bank]] (@thisisnickys)

### "INSANE"
- When it lands: genuine shock on a real capability jump.
- When it fails: overused, it reads as hype, which is off-axis for an anti-slop brand. Use sparingly.
- Worked example: "This 100% uncensored AI model is insane" → [[pattern-bank]] (@davidondrej)

### "EASY"
- When it lands: relief for an audience that finds AI overwhelming.
- When it fails: for sophisticated viewers who read "easy" as oversimplified.
- Worked example: "Building Beautiful Websites with Claude Code Is Too Easy" → [[pattern-bank]] (@nateherk)

### "LAZIEST"
- When it lands: a stronger, more disarming take on "easy," signals minimum effort for the payoff.
- When it fails: when the method is actually involved. The promise sets the bar.
- Worked example: "The Laziest Way to Make Money with Claude" → [[pattern-bank]] (@sabrina_ramonov)

### "RIGHT NOW"
- When it lands: urgency on something genuinely time-sensitive.
- When it fails: when there's no real reason for urgency. Manufactured panic.
- Worked example: "you need to learn MCP RIGHT NOW!!" → [[pattern-bank]] (@networkchuck)

## Audience-specific power words

Pull these when the audience signals are clear. Many double as topic markers that tell the AI viewer "this is for me" in the first frame.

### "CLAUDE"
- When it lands: the single hottest brand term in this niche right now. Instant relevance.
- When it fails: when bolted on with no outcome. Anchor it to a result, not just the name.
- Worked example: "12 Ways to Use Claude So Well It Feels Illegal" → [[pattern-bank]] (@sabrina_ramonov)

### "COWORK"
- When it lands: the specific hot Claude product term. Signals you're current.
- When it fails: cold audiences who don't know what Cowork is yet.
- Worked example: "Every Claude Cowork Concept Explained for Normal People" → [[pattern-bank]] (@brockmesarich)

### "ANTHROPIC"
- When it lands: news/release framing, lends institutional weight.
- When it fails: when the audience cares about the capability, not the company.
- Worked example: "Anthropic Just Dropped Claude for Small Businesses (31 Skills)" → [[pattern-bank]] (@brockmesarich)

### "AGENTS"
- When it lands: signals the frontier, what's next after basic prompting.
- When it fails: for beginners who don't yet know the term.
- Worked example: "AI Agents Full Course 2026: Master Agentic AI" → [[pattern-bank]] (@nicksaraev)

### "AGENTIC WORKFLOWS"
- When it lands: insider phrase that positions you ahead of plain "automation."
- When it fails: for non-technical owners who find it jargon-heavy.
- Worked example: "DON'T build AI automations, build agentic workflows!" → [[pattern-bank]] (@duncanrogoff)

### "AUTOMATION"
- When it lands: the core promise of doing more with less time.
- When it fails: when it sounds technical for a non-technical owner.
- Worked example: "What I'd Learn Instead of Automation in 2026" → [[pattern-bank]] (@nicksaraev)

### "SKILLS"
- When it lands: concrete, collectible, "steal them" energy (Claude Skills).
- When it fails: vague "skills" with no specificity.
- Worked example: "15 Claude Cowork Skills I Can't Live Without" → [[pattern-bank]] (@brockmesarich)

### "MCP"
- When it lands: insider term that signals frontier credibility.
- When it fails: cold beginners won't recognize it.
- Worked example: "you need to learn MCP RIGHT NOW!!" → [[pattern-bank]] (@networkchuck)

### "n8n"
- When it lands: known automation tool, recognizable to the AI-builder crowd.
- When it fails: outside the builder audience it means nothing.
- Worked example: "Claude Managed Agents Just Dropped, And It Kills n8n" → [[pattern-bank]] (@nicksaraev)

### "VEO"
- When it lands: Google's AI-video tool, hot for creators making video.
- When it fails: for audiences not making video.
- Worked example: "How I Use VEO 3 To Create Viral AI Videos In 11 Minutes" → [[pattern-bank]] (@thisisnickys)

### "SORA"
- When it lands: OpenAI's AI-video tool, another creator-specific draw.
- When it fails: for non-video audiences, same as VEO.
- Worked example: "How I Use Sora 2 To Create Viral Videos In 10 Minutes" → [[pattern-bank]] (@thisisnickys)

### "CONTENT"
- When it lands: the bullseye for Billy's positioning (AI to make content).
- When it fails: too broad without a specific outcome attached.
- Worked example: "Claude Just Changed Content Creation Forever!" → [[pattern-bank]] (@sabrina_ramonov)

### "CONTENT TEAM"
- When it lands: the leverage fantasy, a whole team's output from one person.
- When it fails: for solo viewers who don't think in "team" terms yet.
- Worked example: "I Built My Entire Content Team Inside Claude (No Employees)" → [[pattern-bank]] (@thisisnickys)

### "NO EMPLOYEES"
- When it lands: the avatar's exact situation (solo, can't or won't hire).
- When it fails: for audiences that already run teams.
- Worked example: "These 9 AI Businesses Will Make You $1M (With Zero Employees)" → [[pattern-bank]] (@sabrina_ramonov)

### "1-PERSON"
- When it lands: names the solo-owner identity directly.
- When it fails: when paired with an outcome too big to believe from one person.
- Worked example: "How To Start A 1-Person AI Business ($0 to $1M)" → [[pattern-bank]] (@sabrina_ramonov)

### "VIRAL"
- When it lands: the creator's dream outcome, paired with AI video.
- When it fails: when the content can't plausibly go viral. Overpromise.
- Worked example: "How I Made Viral AI Videos in 5 Minutes (Higgsfield AI Tutorial)" → [[pattern-bank]] (@thisisnickys)

### "PERSONAL BRAND"
- When it lands: the avatar's identity (an expert building their name).
- When it fails: rarely for this audience; pair with a contrarian or outcome angle.
- Worked example: "Why Growing A Personal Brand Is An AWFUL Idea" → [[pattern-bank]] (@ed-lawrence)

### "PROMPTS"
- When it lands: concrete, copy-able deliverable. Pairs with a number ("7 prompts").
- When it fails: when the prompts aren't actually shared. "Steal" energy without the goods.
- Worked example: "7 Secret Prompts That Make Claude CODE 10x Better" → [[pattern-bank]] (@sabrina_ramonov)

## Words avoided (flop signals)

- **Fabricated money figures.** Not a single word but a guard: never a dollar claim you can't back. It's the slop the brand fights. See money-proof in [[title-bank]].
- Empty hype with no substance behind it ("GAME CHANGER," "INSANE") when the video doesn't earn it. The anti-slop positioning means the payoff has to match the promise.

Billy adds real flop words here after publishing and seeing what tanks.

## Considered + dropped

None dropped this build. Future refreshes archive dropped words here with rationale.

## Field reference

- **When it lands / When it fails**: the fit criterion and the guard.
- **Worked example**: a real title from the research, linked to [[pattern-bank]].

Fields deliberately not captured: frequency, channels-used, confidence rank. Popularity in the set is not fit for the next title.
